tables.title: Paired date-block sensitivity for the rejected candidate

figures.caption: Coverage of complete six-contract panels at 12:00 local time; peach indicates an excluded event.
Historical spreads from accepted noon events. Candle-close quotes have no accompanying depth or fill guarantee.
Conditional integer-resolution basket gaps from hourly quotes; current fee scenarios do not establish historical execution or contractual arbitrage.
Held-out scores for the market-derived baseline and the rejected calibration candidate. Lower is better; validation selected the baseline.
Pooled reliability bins on held-out events. Contracts within an event are dependent; this curve is descriptive, not an independent-bin significance test.
Displayed-depth purchase costs for the final snapshot whose midpoint is nearest 0.50; the selection rule is descriptive and does not use future returns.
Snapshot imbalance and the next observed midpoint change in the brief live session; these are not order-flow events or independent trading trials.
Six synthetic mechanisms, 500 replications each. Passing known-truth tests verifies selected logic, not real-market profitability.
Synthetic independent leg-fill stresses. A positive expected payoff can coexist with losses when an incomplete basket remains exposed.
Paired date-block confidence intervals for the rejected candidate on later dates; negative differences favour the candidate. The selected method is the baseline itself.

figures.short: Recorded order-book depth in three dimensions
figures.caption: Recorded order-book depth for KXHIGHNY-26OCT18-B56.5. Each line is one REST observation; the surface between observations is not reconstructed.
Calibration sensitivity for KXHIGHNY-26SEP29, the first later-period New York event. T is varied for illustration; the selected research model remains T = 1.
Synthetic six-leg loss probability under independent fills, equally likely winning outcomes and raw quadratic fees. This analytical surface is not an empirical return forecast.
